newsitem.title: CHINA: Eastern Communications sells 156m yuan equipment.
newsitem.headline: Eastern Communications sells 156m yuan equipment.

text.p: CITIC Industrial Bank will lend 156 million yuan ($18.7 million) to Hubei Post and Telecommunication Bureau to buy equipment from Eastern Communications Co, Shanghai Securities News said on Monday.
The cellular phone equipment will be used to enlarge the analog system owned by the Post and Telecommunication Bureau in central Hubei province, the newspaper said.

The loan is termed a buyer credit contract, under which the money can only be used for a specific purpose, it said, adding it was an efficient way to reduce accounts receivable and enlarge market share.
By mid-March, Eastern Communications had signed contracts worth two billion yuan for the sale of base stations for cellular phone systems, it said but gave no further details.

Eastern Communications is China's largest cellular phone maker. It posted net profit of 291.618 million yuan in 1996 based on international accounting standards, up 14.29 percent from 1995's 255.162 million yuan.
Four in every 1,000 people in China have mobile phones, among a population of 1.2 billion, making it the world's fourth largest market after the United States, Japan and Britain.
